name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis; BRIEF ratifies the /spec:mocks approved set) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.81.0 — atlas viewport buttons now rewrite each card's W×H label along with the frame (it was stamped once at load and stayed at the first viewport after switching). Direct patch, no spec — JJ 2026-09-05 at the Hearwell SHAPES look stop. tests/design-atlas.test.js. 7.80.0 — `worktree-include.sh` (`spec-paths worktree-include`) is now the sole owner of copying a host's `.worktreeinclude`-matched gitignored files into a new worktree: `merge-back.sh create` calls it in place of its inline copy block, and `/spec:replay`'s `--setup` now calls it too, before the setup gate runs, so a scratch worktree on a host that boots from env files no longer dies at setup or smoke for a reason unrelated to the reviewer being measured; a host with no manifest is unchanged. `spec-paths` gains the `worktree-include` key. 7.79.0 — `commit-coverage.js` derives commit-time escape coverage in three modes (`--commit`, `--since`, `--repos-root`, `spec-paths commit-coverage`): fix-typed commits (`fix`/`hotfix` type token) joined to File Plan membership plus a preceding `stage:"review"` ledger row name which reviewed spec landed a touched file, distinct from files still in flight under their own spec; fleet mode takes its population from `fleet-reader.js`. `/git:commit` step 3 now runs the commit mode as its offer's oracle instead of the retired git-blame/jq heuristic, offering on any file a reviewed spec landed — still never blocking the commit.
